clue.text: Sense endlessly arresting innocent person's really beginning to rankle

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the saint's letters are held inside
without its end, so the last letter of the word for sense is dropped

parts.note: to sense something is to feel it
a saint is the model innocent person, abbreviated ST

indicators.note: beginning picks out the opening letter of really

explanation.surface: A clean-living person's growing irritation finally comes to a head and starts to grate.
explanation.walkthrough: The saint is the 'innocent person', a crossword staple; the 's is just the surface's possessive and adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance that festers keeps gnawing at you, which is exactly what it does when it rankles.

clue.text: Chap very nearly came a cropper

indicators.note: nearly means short of the end, so each of the two words loses its last letter

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man almost had a nasty tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' works on both words: FELLOW loses its W and VERY loses its Y, leaving FELLO and VER.
explanation.definitionFit: To come a cropper is a British idiom for taking a heavy tumble, hence to topple.

clue.text: Likelier to get upset with each minute stuck in crush

definitions.note: a comparative phrase standing for an adjective; the setter's looseness, as the answer is not itself comparative

indicators.note: stuck in means the pair of abbreviations is pushed inside the word for crush

parts.note: to crush something is to squish it
EA is the standard abbreviation for each, as on price tags

explanation.surface: Someone sensitive is more prone to distress when squeezed in a crowd every minute.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeamish person is easily nauseated or disturbed, more prone than most to be troubled.

clue.text: Edits key conclusion in manuscript

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: in places the word for conclusion inside the abbreviation for manuscript

parts.note: a conclusion is an end

explanation.surface: An editor revises the crucial ending of a draft.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct or revise it, which is what an editor does.

clue.text: Shooting clubs returned by search engine

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for clubs is written backwards

parts.note: bats are clubs used in sport
Bing is Microsoft's search engine

explanation.surface: Golf clubs or guns sent back after an online search.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting pain and a stabbing pain are the same sudden, sharp sensation.

clue.text: Pretend not to see criminal lying stripped under table

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or bent, so the combined letters are rearranged
stripped means the outer layer is taken off, leaving the inner letters of lying

parts.note: the word whose outer letters are removed
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crooked officer feigns ignorance of bribes slipped under the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' leaves YIN from 'lying'; add UNDER and TABLE and 'criminal' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn a blind eye is the idiom for deliberately ignoring something you know is happening.

clue.text: Snub old cricketer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to refuse to deal with or shun
second meaning: Geoffrey ..., the former England and Yorkshire opening batsman

explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott was a celebrated England opening batsman of the 1960s to 1980s; the verb comes from Captain Boycott, an Irish land agent who was ostracised.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun or refuse to take part in something as protest is the common verb sense, alongside the famous surname.

clue.text: Not appropriate to fall asleep during sex

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the nap goes inside

parts.note: IT is a coy word for sex or sex appeal
to nap is to drop off for a short sleep

explanation.surface: Dozing off mid-intimacy would be rather unfitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt is a synonym of unsuitable, the opposite of apt.

clue.text: Gluttonous King George eyed crumble

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, the cipher of King George

indicators.note: to crumble is to break apart, so the letters of eyed are rearranged

explanation.surface: A greedy monarch eyes up a fruit crumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumble' looks like the dessert the king is eyeing, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluttonous and greedy both describe someone with an excessive appetite for food.

clue.text: Bounder's discovered in scandalous exploits

definitions.note: read as 'Bounder is', so the definition is the noun bounder

indicators.note: discovered in means found sitting within these words

explanation.surface: A cad is revealed through his disgraceful behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bounder and louse are both old-fashioned words for a contemptible, dishonourable man.

clue.text: Simon says 'Perhaps Labour's ready to step up'?

parts.note: Labour is an example of a political party, as 'Perhaps' signals
to be game is to be willing to have a go

explanation.surface: A politician named Simon announces his party is prepared to take on more.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon says is a children's game where players obey only orders prefixed with that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon says is a classic children's game played at birthday gatherings, an example of a parlour entertainment.

clue.text: Alarmed by crack in step in building

indicators.note: building means constructing, so these letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is frightened by a fissure in a stair inside a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like a place but is the anagram signal on all of 'crack in step in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic-stricken means seized by sudden fear, an intensified form of being alarmed.

clue.text: Often disheartened with working all the time

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, so only the outer letters of often remain

parts.note: and means with, joining one thing to another
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A discouraged worker is frequently on the job continuously.
explanation.definitionFit: On and on describes something continuing without stopping, endlessly.

clue.text: Trouble with naughty pet daughter's taken on

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaving, so the letters of pet are jumbled

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A family takes in a badly behaved pet, which causes their daughter trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An adopted child or idea is one that has been taken on as one's own.

clue.text: Go out with former lover taking one final jaunt

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: final picks the last letter of jaunt

explanation.surface: Someone goes on a farewell outing with an old flame.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is the act of leaving, and as a verb it means to depart.

clue.text: Carver starts to struggle cutting poultry not completely cooked

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letters of struggle and cutting
cooked suggests something prepared or altered, so the letters are rearranged
not completely means the last letter of poultry is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone carving underdone chicken has a hard time slicing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carver' looks like the person carving the bird, but here it is an artist in stone or wood. The rearranged letters come from the trimmed poultry, after the two starting letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculptor carves figures from stone or wood, so is a carver of a kind.

clue.text: Make a new plan to foster diversity

parts.note: to foster a child is to rear it
a range is a varied spread or diversity

explanation.surface: An organisation reorganises itself to promote inclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange plans is to reschedule or reorganise them, devising a different scheme.

clue.text: Checks out female donkeys?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, fanciful: ass plus the feminine ending -ess, like lioness, made plural

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented word: female asses would be ass-esses, on the model of lionesses.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess something is to evaluate or examine it, matching checks out.

clue.text: Timid man has place taken by soldier

parts.note: HE is the pronoun for a man
to sit is to have a place, as on a committee or in a seat
a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so ant stands for soldier

explanation.surface: A shy man's seat is taken over by a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitant means unsure or holding back, close to shy and lacking in boldness.

clue.text: Almost everyone's in beach shoes

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the beach

parts.note: a beach is often called the sands

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: all means everyone; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: Nearly every holidaymaker is wearing open footwear by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandals are open shoes held on by straps, typical summer footwear.

clue.text: Opening of talks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a narrow mouth or entrance
second meaning: to jaw is to chatter at length

explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening of talks' reads like the start of negotiations; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaws names a gaping mouth or entrance, and as a verb means chatters or gabs.

clue.text: Allege account by copper's occasionally askew

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: occasionally means every other letter, so alternate letters of askew are taken

explanation.surface: A police officer's statement is sometimes off the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal. The alternate letters of askew give SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To accuse someone is to charge or claim that they did wrong, which is to allege.

clue.text: Reptile found in southernmost tip of England

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a scaly four-legged reptile
second meaning: the peninsula in Cornwall that is mainland Britain's southernmost point

explanation.walkthrough: The Lizard is a peninsula in Cornwall, south-west England; Lizard Point is the most southerly point of mainland Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a scaly cold-blooded animal and the Cornish headland at Britain's southern extreme.

clue.text: Shout about Italy's mid-price wine

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for shout goes round the letter for Italy

parts.note: to chant is to call out rhythmically
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: mid picks the middle letter of price

explanation.surface: Someone loudly complains about the cost of a moderately priced Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red from Tuscany, one of Italy's best-known wines.

clue.text: Problem with groups of cells shedding skin

indicators.note: shedding skin means losing the outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: tissues are groups of similar cells in a body

explanation.surface: A biological trouble with cells losing their outer layer.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a point of contention or difficulty, a problem to be dealt with.

clue.text: After regime changes direction, one's leaving the country

indicators.note: After places the direction letter behind the rearranged regime
changes signals the letters of regime are rearranged

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Following a change of government, a woman flees abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An émigrée is a woman who has left her own country to live elsewhere, often for political reasons.

clue.text: Launches new nursing booklet essentially for free

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the anagram wraps round the middle letter
new signals the letters of Launches are made into something new
essentially picks the essence, the central letter of booklet

explanation.surface: Someone releases a fresh pamphlet on nursing at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To unshackle is to release from chains, so to set at liberty.

clue.text: When heading off, pokes fun at relatives

indicators.note: heading off means the head, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: to taunt someone is to mock them

explanation.surface: Family members tease one another as they set out.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunts are relatives: the sisters of one's parents.

clue.text: Service, at the end of the day, is still no good

definitions.text: Service, at the end of the day

parts.note: even so means nevertheless, which is still

explanation.surface: A grumble that, when all is said and done, worship remains worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the end of the day' looks like the idiom for 'ultimately', but it belongs to the definition: an evening service.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican service of evening prayer, held late in the day.

clue.text: Lazy people lied about taking runs on vacation

indicators.note: about here means around or in a different arrangement, so the letters of lied are rearranged
on vacation means emptied out, leaving only the first and last letters of runs

explanation.surface: Slackers who fibbed about doing their exercise runs while away.
explanation.definitionFit: Idlers are people who avoid work, layabouts who are lazy.
